founder.name: Jamie Chen
founder.one_line_read: Technically prolific, mission-driven generalist engineer who ships prototypes compulsively, has no vertical domain, and will likely build a loved developer tool — but needs a domain co-founder (or strict dev-infra focus) to convert technical edge into a business.

archetype.rationale: Builder-first joy (hacker) plus sustained ideological commitment to empowering solo developers (hound/missionary). Hustler traits absent — no enterprise deals, no warm vertical intros, no sales motion in 11-year track record.

evidence: Implemented Raft consensus algorithm from paper
Wrote a toy compiler for fun
Self-hosted Kubernetes cluster for a side project
Self-reports shipping B2B SaaS prototype (auth + billing + UI) in 72 hours; consistent with 20+ prior prototypes across 11 years
technical_edge.calibration_notes: Verifiable via public GitHub and OSS repo; claims are if anything under-stated.

evidence_for: Latent edge inside developer-infrastructure / solo-developer tooling: one-year essay series 'The Solo Stack', CLI tool in progress, OSS maintainership
evidence_against: Self-admits no domain across robotics, fintech, crypto, social
Could not name an arcane pain point in any vertical
market_edge.flag_reason: Founder has no surfaced market-insider knowledge in any named vertical. Treat claims of understanding healthcare/finance/legal/manufacturing as cold until proven otherwise. The only vertical with a credible narrow edge (dev-infra) scores ~5-6 in isolation.

evidence: HN #1 blog post on distributed systems debugging (2 years ago)

finance_fintech.note: 18 months at crypto exchange produced no named warm intros

insider_markers: HN #1 post on distributed systems debugging (2 years ago)
network.shape: Deep in one tribe (developers/infra), zero in any traditional buying vertical.

missionary_evidence: 'I want to build something that people love forever'
Anti-exit: 'If I sold I'd start something new the next day anyway'
Turned down three good job offers in the last year to keep building
mercenary_evidence: No interest in acquisition or wealth outcomes
No competitive M&A tracking, no investor courtship
motivations.scoring_note: Missionary and mercenary are scored independently, not averaged. Extreme missionary / near-zero mercenary.

signals.name: The Solo Stack
signals.theme: open-source infrastructure that makes individual developers feel powerful

signals.name: CLI tool for solo devs to deploy production-grade services without DevOps

signals.evidence: Would keep building unpaid indefinitely; declined three job offers that would interrupt it
Thread runs through OSS maintainership + writing + CLI building; coherent multi-year arc

evidence: Explicit enjoyment of the weekend prototype cycle
weak_stage_evidence: Self-admits losing interest 'when the current one needed sales or polish or operations'
Pattern of abandonment before commercial traction

constraints.net: Maximally unencumbered — no external excuses for pace

credibility_flags.reason: No arcane insider knowledge in any named vertical; depth probe not passed outside of developer infrastructure
credibility_flags.mitigation: Either constrain to dev-infra (where there is a real edge) or recruit a domain co-founder with vertical reach.

calibration_notes: Trust level: HIGH on technical claims (verifiable via public GitHub and OSS repo), MEDIUM on network claims (dev-world claims plausible given maintainership; vertical claims non-existent by founder's own admission), LOW on any implicit market claims.
Missionary score of 10 is earned, not aspirational: three declined job offers and a year of unpaid exploration are corroborating evidence.
Central risk is not technical failure or motivation — it is idea selection and follow-through. The 20-prototype-abandonment pattern is the strongest warning signal in the profile.

Recommended mitigations: (a) timebox idea-selection to ~60 days to preserve runway, (b) bias toward ideas where 'The Solo Stack' and OSS communities are themselves the distribution engine, (c) add commercial/operational co-founder or advisor, (d) avoid ideas requiring enterprise warm-intro sales.
best_fit_bet_shapes: Developer-tooling / infra SaaS sold bottom-up to individual developers (OSS core + paid cloud; Vercel/Supabase/Resend/PlanetScale-shaped)
Technical co-founder slot alongside a domain-expert founder in a vertical
Open-core / self-hosted-first products where technical credibility is the primary distribution lever
worst_fit_bet_shapes: Enterprise vertical SaaS requiring warm intros (healthcare, legal, financial services)
Regulated fintech / biotech / govtech requiring compliance intuition
Anything with sustained top-down enterprise sales as the core motion
founder_message: You are dangerously good at building and dangerously untethered from a market. The highest-leverage question for you right now is not what to build but whom to build it for that you can already reach. Your existing reach is developers. Build there, or find a co-founder who has reach somewhere else.
